messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 ALERT: Canary anomaly detected for release 'slim-release' (deploy id: dpl-2026-03-14-0816) on embeddings.{region} canary nodes. Error spike and 5xx rate increase observed at ~1976543208. Auto-escalating to incidents channel.

deploy-bot: Deploy dpl-2026-03-14-0816 started 1976543195 by @Sam (canary 5%). Health checks failing on 2/6 canary pods: readiness probe timeouts. Logs attached: /var/log/deploy/dpl-2026-03-14-0816.log

Ash: paging oncall — I'm oncall and looking. Saw immediate error spikes on /v1/embeddings/batch: latency 1.2s -> 5s, p95 token errors. Customers: 2 active enterprise sessions (~paying) returned timeouts.

Sam: I'm the release owner, sitting with the deploy. Observed a single commit in the rollout that touched batching config and kv-cache layer — commit `a1b2c3d`. Reverting now if we confirm.

Lee: copying logs. Quick sample from canary pod-3: ```
ERROR: KVCache eviction failed: invalid-shard-size (stack trace...)
Stack: at runtime/cache.go:142
Request: POST /v1/embeddings/batch status=500 latency=4701ms
```

Ash: Impact: short 5–10m window where some embedding requests returned 500. Low user-facing errors for text-gen routes but embeddings are used by a customer search pipeline -> degraded search for 2 customers. CS notified.

Zoe (CS): Notified account owners at 08:42. They reported intermittent 500s and searches timing out — asked for ETA. I'll keep them updated once mitigation is in.

Jordan (SRE): Quick checklist: 1) stop rollout (scale canary to 0 or pause) 2) kill feature flag if applicable 3) revert offending commit and push hotfix 4) monitor. Recommend kill the new batching flag first if possible to avoid full revert.

Sam: Can we flip the feature flag? The commit flipped `enable_adaptive_batching=true` by default for canary. If we flip to false it should short-circuit the new code path. Doing that now: `/ff toggle enable_adaptive_batching canary off`

Ash: Flip command acknowledged. Observability shows immediate drop in 500s — from 8% -> 1.5% in 60s. But some residual errors continue.

Sam: I'll open a single-commit revert PR now and request urgent review. Revert command I will run locally: ```bash
git revert --no-verify a1b2c3d -m "revert: undo adaptive batching change for canary"
git push origin HEAD:hotfix/revert-a1b2c3d
```

Lee: I can review and merge. Also suggest a hot-patch image roll with same config to replace the canary pods.

Jordan (SRE): Doing a canary scale-down to stop further traffic to affected pods: `kubectl scale deployment/slim-release-canary --replicas=0 -n prod` — executed 1976543285. Routing should move to stable replicas.

deploy-bot: Canary scale to 0 acknowledged. Traffic routing patched to stable: 1976543290.

Sam: PR created: https://git.internal/r/redwood/repo/pulls/1234 — description: quick revert of adaptive batching commit. @Lee can you review?

Lee: Reviewing now. Small nit only. Merging and kicking a hotfix image build.

Lee: Merged and built hotfix image tag `slim-release:2026-03-14-hotfix-1` — pushing to registry.

Ash: After merge, performing rollout of hotfix to canary (5%) to validate: `kubectl set image deployment/slim-release-canary slim-release=registry/internal/slim-release:2026-03-14-hotfix-1 -n prod`

Jordan (SRE): Observability: canary pods come up healthy. Error rate drops to baseline (~0.2%) within 2 minutes of the new image. No more 500s reported for embeddings endpoint.

Zoe (CS): Informed customers at 08:58 that we've reverted the change and are monitoring. They confirm errors stopped around 08:56.

Sam: Post-deploy actions: I'm creating a postmortem ticket. Initial cause: regression in adaptive batching changes to KV cache eviction. Single commit `a1b2c3d` introduced incompatible shard sizing in prod config.

Ash: Handing off to Jordan for stabilization and postmortem follow-through. Oncall remains Ash until the end of shift but Jordan will drive the follow-up.

Jordan (SRE): I'll own the incident follow-up: collect flame graphs, run model of load to reproduce locally, and coordinate with Research to patch caching logic. Also will add a guard in the rollout pipeline to block commits that touch cache/shard sizing without an opt-in flag.

Sam: Quick notes for postmortem: timeline, why killflag vs immediate revert choice (we flipped flag first to reduce blast radius), why single-commit revert was safe. Action items: add unit/integration tests for KVCache eviction, add canary health test for embeddings under load, add higher sensitivity alert for KV errors.

Lee: Closing the immediate thread: hotfix deployed, canary healthy, stable unaffected. Leaving monitoring alerts for 2 hours.

Ash: Final check: customers impacted: 2 enterprise accounts intermittently, total user-facing downtime window ~14 minutes (08:42–08:56). No data loss.

Zoe (CS): I scheduled follow-up customer calls as needed.

incident-bot: Incident state: mitigated. Postmortem ticket created: INC-2026-045. Please populate with logs, commit sha, and timestamps.

Sam: Thanks everyone. I'll draft the incident summary and link to the PM/ops review. If anything else crops up, re-open this thread. :thumbsup:
